summary: Round 2's four answers hold where they are mechanical -- the text-block escape branch is correct against every Java form I could construct, the 36-entry list matches the 36 samples, the counts in the State cell (36 banned, 103 tracked src/main, 11 implements-matches, 2 in binstore-backends, 1 real-tree match in LocalFsBinStore) all verify, and the real tree reports 101 files. But the central claim the round added -- that the construct families are now CLOSED AT THE FAMILY -- is false for the two families it names by name, and I again wrote compiling business-logic files that reach a real TLS socket, a real UDP socket, the wall clock, the monotonic clock and the filesystem while the gate prints ok. Separately, the round REMOVED two deny-list entries (.openStream(, .openConnection() against a hypothetical false positive and replaced them with .toURL(, which is a strictly narrower shape; I measured the coverage that was lost, and the justification recorded in the backlog is factually wrong.

findings.title: "the families are now closed at the family" is false for SocketFactory./ServerSocketFactory. and for the X.now( family; a compiling business-logic file reaches a real TLS socket, a real UDP socket, both clocks and the filesystem and the gate prints ok

the round DELETED .openStream( and .openConnection( from the deny-list against a hypothetical false positive; the coverage lost is real and measured, and the reason recorded in the backlog is factually wrong
Clock. has an empty member, so it bans naming the seam type as well as sourcing it, and the real clock now has nowhere legal to be constructed
findings.failure_scenario:
_shape('Clock.') yields the regex \bClock\s*(?:\.|::)\s* with an EMPTY tail, so it matches any member access on the type -- including Clock.class, which names a type and sources nothing. That is the one distinction the scanner header, the gate header, AGENTS.md and code-structure.md all say this gate preserves ('it bans SOURCING a real instance ... never NAMING a seam type').

The live consequence is that Clock.systemUTC() now has no legal home. Every one of the ~20 occurrences in this tree is under src/test, src/clusterTest or src/testFixtures; no src/main file sources a real clock yet because there is no composition root (`git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*Main*.java'` is empty). When the ingester's bootstrap lands it must write Clock.systemUTC() somewhere under src/main, the gate will refuse it, and the only remedy the failure message offers is 'it belongs in binstore-backends -- which is a module move and an argument', which is wrong advice for a composition root: its job is sourcing real instances, not object-store I/O. By the gate's own argument ('a gate that refuses correct code is one an author edits rather than obeys') that is the weakening pressure it warns about, aimed at the next milestone. Worth either an exempt path for the composition root or a backlog row saying it is coming.

verified_from_earlier_rounds: Round 2 major (escaped \""" inside a text block blanks the rest of the file): FIXED and correct. I walked the round-3 branch against \\ before the delimiter, \" before it, an odd run of backslashes, a line-continuation backslash, EOF inside the block, and an empty-string pair adjacent to a string opener; each stops where Java stops. The pin anESCAPEDDelimiterInsideATextBlockDoesNotBlankTheRestOfTheFile reds on the old behaviour.

Round 1 test findings T1/T2/T3: CLOSED. T1 (13 of 16 entries deletable) is killed by everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED's containsExactlyInAnyOrderElementsOf against io_seam_scan.BANNED read out of the scanner itself -- deleting an entry now reds the coverage assertion, not just a sample. T2 (delete CHAR from the tuple) and T3 (drop re.S from BLOCK) are structurally gone: code_only is a single left-to-right pass with no tuple and no BLOCK regex, and both routes are pinned by aCHARLiteralHoldingAQuoteDoesNotBlindTheScanner and the multi-line-javadoc arm of aBannedCallQUOTEDInACommentOrALiteralIsNotAViolation.

Round 2 minor (success line overstating): FIXED. The line now reads '101 business-logic file(s) name none of the 36 banned constructs (full tree: 869 tracked/staged)' -- it claims naming, not seam-taking, and the 36 is read from BANNED at runtime rather than hardcoded.

Round 2 minor (LocalSequencer superlative): the superlative is gone from scripts/check-io-seam.sh, docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md and docs/internal/product/backlog.md. Not raised as a finding; noting it so it is not mistaken for a fifth site.

Every number in the State cell, the scanner header, the gate header and the test javadoc VERIFIED in the worktree: len(BANNED)=36; git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java' = 103; non-adapter = 101 and the gate prints 101; files matching implements .*(BinStore|Sequencer|SubscriptionTransport|Membership|Clock) = 11; binstore-backends src/main = 2; scanning all 103 including the adapter matches exactly one file, LocalFsBinStore, and nothing else; the glob covers all eight modules (binstore-backends, binstore-spi, client, format, http, ingest, plugin, sequencer).
